title: A fair discovery and releasing a structure
meaning: Your union can see a familiar arrangement’s weakness when fairness helps acknowledge attachment to it without requiring everything to remain unchanged.
text: In the physical position, Justice expresses your partnership’s fair actions and responsibility for consequences. In energy, the Tower describes tension around an assumption that no longer withstands scrutiny. In emotions, the Devil conveys attachment narrowing freedom: a familiar structure feels difficult to release even when its weakness is visible. Honest discovery and readiness to change may not arrive together. You can acknowledge that difference without accusing each other of deliberate insincerity. Recognising what is unsound can remain a real step even while feelings still hold tightly to the certainty that the old form once provided.

For example, a familiar household list turns out barely to include preparation. The old balance loses credibility, yet changing the routine feels worrying because at least it is understood. **Admitting a structure’s weakness does not immediately remove attachment to it.** One part can be refined and tested through experience. You need not dismiss the entire past to make room for a fair correction or discover what genuinely deserves preserving.

Attachment strengthens if familiarity proves necessity. An arrangement worked before, so another supposedly only complicates life. Seeking certainty, you use previous effort against change. Fairness guards restriction. Freedom grows when the loss of familiarity can be named alongside trying an alternative. Immediate relief is not required, but its absence need not become an obligation permanently to remain in an arrangement that no longer fits.
